[ASSISTANT_SAID] These statutes include the Evidence Act 1995 (Cth) and Evidence Act 1995 (NSW), among others.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The uniform evidence law is not a national law, but it is widely adopted across Australia.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Queensland, South Australia, and Western Australia have not adopted the uniform evidence law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The seven jurisdictions that have adopted the law account for the majority of Australia's court systems and population.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] There have been no new Australian entries to the scheme since 2011.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Non-adopting jurisdictions are in a form of limbo, while adopting jurisdictions face challenges in implementing the scheme.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] This third edition will continue to cover only the adopting jurisdictions.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Attention is needed to the earlier law and legislative and judicial divergences in the uniform scheme.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The basic features of the uniform evidence law are introduced in this chapter.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The scheme is characterized by its continuity with earlier traditions of evidence law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The scheme aims to provide a broadly applicable, uniformly developed, and easily found Australian evidence law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Connections between the uniform evidence law and other laws are detailed, including local statutes, common law, overseas law, and human rights law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The uniform evidence law is a complex and constantly evolving area of law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Legal professionals and scholars need to stay up to date with developments in the uniform evidence law and related fields.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The uniform evidence law is not a radical departure from the previous law.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Australian evidence law has always been a set of procedural rules that limit the freedom of parties and courts to present and find facts.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The basic structure of the uniform evidence law includes rules for courtroom events, exceptions and sub-exceptions to the rule of relevance, and mild controls on the outcomes of evidence use.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] This structure is identical to the approach of the common law, though the form is different.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The primary purpose of Australian evidence law is to promote the accuracy of legal fact-finding.
